verdict_reason: The 9d removal of the legacy no-id fallback fixes F72-1 and F72-2 outright: the cap pair is built only from id-carrying rows deduped by exact consult id with the 24 h bound applied at read time inside endpoint_health, the negatives (>1 h apart, slow 429, no-id rows, 25 h-old hits) are pinned by tests, and the only residuals found are documented design policy.
reply_markdown:
## Answers

**Q1 — paths beyond the documented residual.** None found. Verified in code: the pair is built only from rows with a non-empty `consult_id` (`crates/c3-core/src/health.rs:1142`), deduped by exact id (`health.rs:1148-1154`), and every hit must be younger than 24 h at read time (`health.rs:1143`) — the filter lives inside `endpoint_health`, so `plan_cap_verdict` and every provider/preflight read inherit it (the providers test goes through `endpoint_health`, `crates/c3/src/providers.rs:3375`). The 100-character text comparison is gone. Negatives are pinned: no-id rows never complete a pair (`plan.rs:478-497`), hits 25 h old uncounted at read time (`plan.rs:517-536`), >1 h apart (`plan.rs:654`), slow 5 s 429 (`plan.rs:661`). Two consequences remain, both design rather than defects (filed as notes): (a) repeats inside ONE consultation share the id and count once, so exhaustion observed only within a single consultation stays on the plain 10-minute burst; (b) a non-empty `reset_hint` that never resolves (`next_cap_reset` → None, e.g. `monthly:99…`) falls back to second hit + 24 h while the pair actually dissolves at first hit + 24 h — only the refusal text can overstate the outage, by at most the pair gap.

**Q2 — ACCEPT (tag v0.2.2).** F72-1 (read-time bound) and F72-2 (identity, not text prefix) are fixed by removal, not refinement; the test suite covers the identity rule, the read-time bound and every negative; the requested checks (workspace tests 828 passed, clippy/fmt clean, harness 125/0) are green. Findings #1 and #2 are notes, not blockers.

findings.claim: All instant-429 rows from one consultation share its consult_id and count as a single hit, so cap exhaustion that only ever surfaces inside a single consultation (retries or multiple reviewer attempts of one run) can never complete the pair and stays on the plain 10-minute burst.
findings.trigger: One consultation makes two instant-429 attempts on a capped-plan endpoint; no second consultation fails.

evidence.observation: Dedup skips any row whose consult_id is already in seen_ids, so same-id rows contribute one hit regardless of how many attempts they represent.
The machine record's consult_id is copied from the ledger entry's consultation id, so every row of one consultation carries the same id.

findings.verification: Run a single consultation whose two reviewer attempts both fail as instant 429s on a capped entry and assert the entry keeps ordinary burst handling (no 'plan quota' verdict).
findings.remedy: None required - it is the documented 'same id = one hit' rule; optionally state this consequence in the wave note's residual paragraph.

findings.claim: When a non-empty reset_hint never resolves (next_cap_reset returns None, e.g. 'monthly:99T00:00+08:00'), the displayed until falls back to second hit + 24 h while the read-time bound dissolves the pair at first hit + 24 h, so the refusal text can overstate the outage by up to the pair gap (max 60 min); the verdict itself flips to available correctly because the aged-out hit leaves len < 2.
findings.trigger: A roster entry carries a syntactically accepted reset_hint for which next_cap_reset always returns None, and two id-carrying instant 429s land within an hour.

evidence.observation: unhinted branch uses first + 24 h (matching the read-time bound), but the None fallback of the hinted branch uses second_utc + 24 h.
Not checked whether roster validation rejects such never-resolving hints; if it does, the path is unreachable.

findings.verification: Check validate_roster against 'monthly:99T00:00+08:00'; if accepted, run plan_cap_verdict with two hits 60 min apart and compare v.until with the instant the pair ages out at read time.
findings.remedy: Use first.with_timezone(&Utc) + Duration::hours(24) in the None fallback too, matching the unhinted branch.

first_run_checklist: A fresh 429 failure appears in both the repository ledger and the machine health file carrying the same consult_id (the machine record mirrors the ledger id).
After upgrading, a retained pre-9b no-id machine row alone never produces a 'plan quota: 429 twice' outage in providers list or panel output.

Two genuinely distinct consultations hitting instant 429s within an hour on a capped entry produce 'plan quota: 429 twice in N min, no window text; retry after <instant>' with the retry instant matching reset_hint (or first hit + 24 h when no hint is set).
A successful explicit run after such an outage clears it (the operator override), and an unhinted entry becomes eligible again 24 h after the pair's first hit.
